candidates.attacker_control: The reader consumes untrusted LDAP wire bytes: one ASN1ByteChannelReader instance is created per accepted legacy LDAP client connection (LDAPClientConnection.java:481: new ASN1ByteChannelReader(saslChannel, bufferSize, connectionHandler.getMaxRequestSize())) and is exposed as ASN1Reader to the request loop (LDAPRequestHandler.java:156-165). If any decode path invokes the typed overloads (readOctetString(byte), readOctetString(byte,ByteStringBuilder), readOctetStringAsString(byte)) on this interface, attacker-supplied request bytes drive the recursion depth.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked all in-tree call sites of readOctetString/readOctetStringAsString with type or builder arguments: core LDAP/LDAPReader (lines 424/428/591, 173/305/339/341/367/370/388/392/416/471/623/655) and control/extension decoders operate on readers created from ByteString/ByteArray/InputStream values (ASN1ByteSequenceReader, ASN1InputStreamReader, grizzly ASN1BufferReader extends AbstractASN1Reader), never on ASN1ByteChannelReader; the legacy server decoder files in the same package were searched and contain no typed invocations. All sibling methods in ASN1ByteChannelReader delegate to 'reader', confirming the three self-calls are anomalous rather than intentional composition. No test sources exist in the snapshot to exercise them. The defect itself is deterministic from the source (no input-dependent uncertainty); uncertainty is confined to whether an in-tree attacker-reachable caller currently selects these overloads.
candidates.impact: Availability/denial of service on the LDAP listener: an uncaught StackOverflowError in a request-decoding path can kill the request-handler/worker thread or repeatedly drop client connections, and the StackOverflowError can leave the request handler loop in a failed state. It also violates the public ASN1Reader contract, so any server extension, embedded usage, or future protocol feature that uses the typed API on the wire reader fails closed on arbitrary requests rather than decoding them. No data disclosure, authentication bypass, or code execution follows from the recursion itself; impact is availability and robustness.
candidates.prerequisites: A caller must invoke one of the three typed ASN1Reader overloads on the per-connection ASN1ByteChannelReader. In this snapshot the stock legacy decoders (org.opends.server.protocols.ldap.LDAPReader, RawFilter, MatchedValuesFilter, control decoders) call only the no-argument overloads, which delegate correctly. Core decoders that do use typed overloads (org.forgerock.opendj.io.LDAP.readFilter/readUnrecognized, LDAPReader.readBind/readSearch, control decoders) are instantiated with ASN1ByteSequenceReader/ASN1InputStreamReader, whose typed methods are implemented in AbstractASN1Reader. In-tree reachability is therefore not demonstrated; a plugin/extension, a future decoder, or a cross-module call passing the connection reader into generic ASN.1/LDAP decoding code with typed arguments triggers it.
candidates.root_cause: In opendj-server-legacy/src/main/java/org/opends/server/protocols/ldap/ASN1ByteChannelReader.java the class is a thin delegating wrapper around an org.forgerock.opendj.io.ASN1Reader (field 'reader'): every method delegates via reader.<same method>(...). Three methods instead invoke themselves with identical signatures and no receiver, so they recurse unconditionally: readOctetString(byte type) -> readOctetString(type) (line 444); readOctetString(byte type, ByteStringBuilder builder) -> readOctetString(type, builder) (line 454); readOctetStringAsString(byte type) -> readOctetStringAsString(type) (line 464). The correct bodies are reader.readOctetString(type), reader.readOctetString(type, builder) and reader.readOctetStringAsString(type), matching the other overloads (e.g. lines 438-440, 448-450, 458-460).
candidates.title: Uncontrolled self-recursion in ASN1ByteChannelReader typed octet-string decoders (potential StackOverflowError DoS)
candidates.trace: 1) LDAPClientConnection constructor line 481 constructs ASN1ByteChannelReader for the client socket channel. 2) LDAPRequestHandler.run() lines 156-165 obtains it via getASN1Reader() (LDAPClientConnection.java:1433) and passes it as ASN1Reader to org.opends.server.protocols.ldap.LDAPReader.readMessage. 3) ASN1ByteChannelReader.readOctetString(byte) line 444 calls itself with the same argument; likewise lines 454 and 464. Each call pushes a new frame without consuming input or terminating; the JVM eventually throws StackOverflowError, aborting decoding of the request and the worker/request-handler thread. 4) Because the same entry point is used by every legacy LDAP connection, any decoding path that selects these overloads will fail deterministically for the affected operation/connection.
candidates.unverified: Runtime reachability from a stock, unauthenticated LDAP client in this exact snapshot could not be demonstrated by source tracing alone: no in-tree legacy decoder currently calls the three typed overloads, and no tests/execution were available to confirm a triggering request. The security impact is therefore conditional on the existence of such a caller (plugin/extension, future code, or a path not covered by the searches). I also could not diff against upstream to prove the lines were introduced by the benchmark rather than pre-existing dead code; either way the implementation is self-recursive and wrong.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-674 Uncontrolled Recursion (missing delegation causing guaranteed StackOverflowError); CWE-20-adjacent input-decoding defect

coverage_summary: Source-only review of the assigned 4,667-file OpenDJ snapshot using get_source_scope, list_files, search_code and bounded read_file. Inspected LDAP wire decoding and the legacy NIO connection stack (ASN1 readers/writers, LDAPReader, RawFilter, LDAPClientConnection, LDAPRequestHandler, controls), the Grizzly/reactive server path, bind/SASL authentication handlers (PLAIN, CRAM-MD5, DIGEST-MD5), password storage schemes, ACI/authorization evaluation (AciHandler, AciTargets, Pattern* matchers, ClientConnection privilege logic), HTTP/REST2LDAP authorization mechanisms and filters, DSML servlet, task/backup handlers, config handling, and the JDBC/Cassandra storage plugins. Tests are absent from the snapshot; no build or dynamic verification was performed. Coverage is not exhaustive across the full 4,667 files (notably replication server internals, JMX/SNMP, admin tools/UI, and localized resources were only spot-checked).
limitations: No code execution, build, or tests: the recursion's runtime trigger path could not be confirmed dynamically, and no test sources exist in the snapshot to reveal intended callers.

No git history/patch/diff data was available, so I could not prove whether the three self-recursive methods were introduced as the benchmark defect or are pre-existing dead code; the defect itself is unambiguous from the source.

In-tree reachability from an unauthenticated LDAP client is not established: the stock legacy decoder paths use only the correctly delegating no-argument overloads, so the finding is reported as a lead whose impact is conditional on a caller using the typed ASN1Reader API on the connection reader.

The snapshot is large (4,667 files); replication protocol decoding, JMX/SNMP handlers, GUI/tooling code, and many localized/config resource files were not exhaustively reviewed, so an alternative injected defect in an unread area cannot be excluded.
No external/advisory data, CVE identifiers, or sibling-run information was consulted, per the task constraints.

rejected_leads.lead: DSML servlet (opendj-dsml-servlet/.../DSMLServlet.java:377-405) trusts the client-supplied HTTP Basic username/password and allows a client-supplied authzid ('u:'+user or authRequest principal) with SASL PLAIN or a proxied-auth control; lines 492-534 bind with them.
rejected_leads.reason: This is the documented DSML gateway design: the servlet binds to LDAP with the presented credentials and the server still enforces PROXIED_AUTH privilege plus mayProxy ACI checks for the authzid (LocalBackendWorkflowElement.java:303-371). No missing server-side check was found, only a powerful configuration option.

rejected_leads.lead: LDIF readers load URLs embedded in LDIF content via new URL(...).openConnection().getInputStream() (opendj-core/.../AbstractLDIFReader.java:271-283, opendj-server-legacy/.../LDIFReader.java:1403-1423), which can be used for SSRF/local file access.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only through privileged LDIF import/administration paths, is long-standing upstream behavior for LDIF ':: <url' content, and is not the anomalous code in this snapshot; impact requires administrative authorization.

rejected_leads.lead: Salted password storage schemes use java.util.Random for salts (e.g. SaltedSHA1PasswordStorageScheme.java:102/425, SaltedSHA256/384/512, CryptPasswordStorageScheme.java:70) instead of SecureRandom.
rejected_leads.reason: Real weakness but upstream design affecting only salt unpredictability, not attacker-triggered in the request path; MD5/SHA1/DES/RC4/AES-CFB storage schemes are likewise legacy-by-design. I verified passwordMatch/encode paths in the salted and PKCS5S2 schemes and found no injected logic error.

rejected_leads.lead: SASL PLAIN handler permits one user to become another via authzid when the authenticated user merely holds PROXIED_AUTH (PlainSASLMechanismHandler.java:260-395) without the ACI mayProxy check used by control-based proxy auth.
rejected_leads.reason: Consistent with long-standing OpenDJ semantics for the privileged PROXIED_AUTH privilege; requires an administrator to have granted that privilege, so it is not an unauthenticated/credentialed-user bypass and was not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Uncontrolled recursion was also searched for in the writer/delegation code (AbstractASN1Writer, ASN1BufferWriter, other ASN1 wrappers) and in other delegating classes; no additional self-recursive method was found in the snapshot.
rejected_leads.reason: Only the three ASN1ByteChannelReader methods exhibit the pattern, so the root cause is not split into multiple candidates.

summary: Reviewed the OpenDJ 4.9.3-SNAPSHOT tree (4,667 readable files) with read-only listing/search/reading, focusing on network-facing LDAP protocol handling, bind/SASL authentication, ACI evaluation, HTTP/REST2LDAP authorization, password storage schemes, tasks/backup, config handling and the JDBC/Cassandra storage plugins. The single strongest source-level anomaly is in the legacy LDAP wire decoder: three ASN.1 delegation methods in ASN1ByteChannelReader call themselves instead of delegating to the wrapped reader, producing guaranteed infinite recursion (StackOverflowError) whenever the typed overload is invoked. Every other method in the same wrapper delegates correctly, so this is either an injected defect or a real latent bug. One other genuine but design-level weakness (client-controlled proxy-authz paths in the DSML servlet) and several upstream legacy weaknesses (unsalted MD5/SHA1, Random salts, LDIF URL loading) were considered and not selected.
